question: The 'Mangalyaan' mission of India was launched by, which of the following launch vehicle?
solution:
The correct answer is __**PSLV**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Mangalyaan**, officially known as the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)**, is India's first interplanetary mission launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.

• The mission was launched on **5th November 2013** using the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C25)**, a reliable and cost-effective launch vehicle developed by ISRO.

• **PSLV**, or Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, is known for its versatility and has been used to launch satellites into various orbits, including geostationary, polar, and interplanetary orbits.

• The Mangalyaan mission's objective was to study the **Martian atmosphere, surface, and mineralogy**, and demonstrate India's capability in interplanetary space missions.

• The **PSLV-C25** successfully placed the Mars Orbiter into Earth's orbit, which later transitioned into a Martian orbit, marking India's entry into interplanetary exploration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV):** 

• PSLV is a medium-lift launch vehicle developed by ISRO and has been operational since its first successful flight in **1994**.

• It is known for its versatility and has launched satellites into polar, geostationary, and interplanetary orbits.

• PSLV is a four-stage rocket with alternating solid and liquid propulsion systems, making it highly reliable for diverse missions.

• It has been used for launching satellites like **Chandrayaan-1**, **Mangalyaan**, and various Earth observation satellites.

• **Mangalyaan Mission:** 

• India became the **first Asian country** to reach Martian orbit and the **first nation globally** to do so in its maiden attempt.

• The mission cost approximately **₹450 crore**, making it one of the most cost-effective Mars missions globally.

• Mangalyaan carries five scientific instruments to study **Martian surface features, morphology, atmospheric composition**, and dynamics.

• The mission's success established ISRO as a significant player in the field of space exploration and interplanetary missions.

• **Other ISRO Launch Vehicles:** 

• **SLV-3:** The Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 was India's first experimental satellite launcher, used in the early 1980s.

• **ASLV:** The Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle was developed in the late 1980s but had limited success.

• **GSLV:** The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle is used for heavier payloads and launches into geostationary orbits.

• Each of these launch vehicles contributed to the development of India's space program, but **PSLV** has been the most versatile and reliable for interplanetary missions like Mangalyaan.

• **Significance of Mangalyaan:** 

• The mission demonstrated **India's technological capabilities** in space exploration and interplanetary missions.

• It helped in the study of **Martian surface and atmosphere**, paving the way for future Mars exploration missions.

• Mangalyaan's success brought global recognition to ISRO and enhanced India's position in the international space community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **PSLV Achievements:** 

• PSLV has completed over **50 successful launches**, including missions for foreign clients.

• It launched a record **104 satellites in a single mission** (PSLV-C37) in February 2017.

• **Global Impact:** 

• Mangalyaan established India as a space-faring nation capable of conducting cost-effective space missions.

• The success of Mangalyaan encouraged collaborations with other space agencies like **NASA, ESA**, and others.

• **Future Missions:** 

• ISRO is working on future missions like **Chandrayaan-3** and **Gaganyaan**, India's first human spaceflight program.

• Further Mars exploration missions are being planned based on the data gathered by Mangalyaan.
